statements.t: “Our team continues to deliver exceptional project execution, which along with an increasing mix of fabrication work, contributed to the delivery of the highest Adjusted EBITDA margin in company history.
Our confidence in the fundamentals of our business is reflected in our increased guidance for this year, and growth embedded in our initial 2027 guidance.
This outlook also underpins the Board’s authorization of our $150 million stock repurchase program, which broadens our capital allocation options.”

Engineering & Consulting segment revenue for the third quarter 2026 totaled $199.9 million, a decrease of (5.8)% from $212.2 million for the third quarter 2025, driven by a decline in Program & Project Management services and modestly lower Engineering & Design revenue, primarily from education clients.

The increase in non-GAAP Adjusted Gross Margin was primarily driven by higher project margins in our Program & Project Management service line, and a favorable revenue mix shift toward Engineering & Design.

The increase in non-GAAP Adjusted Gross Margin was primarily driven by higher project margins in our Installation & Fabrication service line and greater economies of scale in customer fulfillment support costs, partially offset by a revenue mix shift toward our Installation & Fabrication service line and lower project margins in our Maintenance & Service service line.

We are excited to welcome CTI to our team, and look forward to expanding our service reach and accelerating our growth together in this geography.” For the calendar year 2026, CTI is expected to generate revenue of approximately $40 million, of which Legence expects to record approximately $6 to $8 million of revenue during the fourth quarter of 2026.

In early November 2026, the Company’s Board of Directors authorized a $150 million share repurchase plan, reflecting the Company’s strong financial position and outlook, as well as a commitment to a disciplined approach to capital allocation.

The new share repurchase plan will be executed in accordance with applicable securities laws and regulations, does not require any specific number of shares to be acquired, and may be suspended or discontinued at any time at the Company’s discretion.
A replay of the webcast can be accessed through the same webcast link on the Company’s website shortly after the call and will be available through December 12, 2026.

Due to the high variability and difficulty in making accurate forecasts and projections of some of the information excluded from these projected measures, together with some of the excluded information not being ascertainable or accessible, the Company is unable to quantify certain amounts that would be required to be included in the most directly comparable GAAP financial measures without unreasonable effort.

We believe that backlog and awarded contracts and book-to-bill ratio enable us to more effectively forecast our future results and working capital needs, as well as better identify future operating trends that may not otherwise be apparent.
Backlog represents, as of any date of determination, the expected revenue values of the remaining performance obligations under our contracted fixed-price projects.

Awarded contracts represents, as of any date of determination, the expected revenue values of projects awarded to us following a request for proposals but for which a formal contract has not yet been signed.

the business plans or financial condition of our customers
the impact of acquired companies, including Bowers, on our organization and the ability to recognize the anticipated benefits of such acquisitions
the regulations related to environmental, health and safety matters
the ability to receive necessary government permits and approvals
the future availability and price of materials and equipment necessary for the performance of our business
the risks associated with inflation, interest rates, recessionary economic conditions and commodity prices
the fact that we outsource various elements of the services we sell and use materials and equipment produced by third parties
our clients’ reliance on third party financing
the recognition of all revenues from our backlog and awarded contracts
our receipt of all payments anticipated under awarded projects and customer contracts
the maintenance of safe work sites and equipment
restrictions imposed by our existing and any future indebtedness
our exposure to costs and liabilities under environmental, health and safety laws
misconduct and errors by employees, subcontractors, partners or third party service providers
